headline: Recommended approval of a lease for News Café's parking lot on Broad and North Union streets, and an easement at 100 Freight Street.
summary: The lease runs six months, then month-to-month, and the committee found no issues with it. As of the meeting, Narragansett Electric had not directly responded to the city's changes to the easement. Under the vote, City Solicitor Frank J. Milos, Jr. will negotiate any concerns and bring major changes back to the committee.
decisions: Recommended approval of a six-month lease, then month-to-month, with Joshua Café, LLC d/b/a News Café, on a 3-0 roll call vote.
Recommended approval of the Narragansett Electric easement at 100 Freight Street on a 3-0 roll call vote, with the city solicitor to negotiate any concerns.

Easement with Narragansett Electric at 100 Freight Street
plain_text:
PAWTUCKET CITY COUNCIL 
CITY PROPERTY COMMITTEE 
OCTOBER 21, 2026 
 
A meeting of the City Council City Property Committee was held on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, 
at 6:33 p.m., in the City Council Conference Room, Room 140, 100 Freight Street, Pawtucket, RI. 
 
Present – Councilor Stachowiak, Chair; Councilors Araujo and Moreno. 
 
Absent – 0. 
 
Councilor Stachowiak presided. 
 
Also present were Chris Crawley, Acting Director of Public Works ; and Frank J. Milos, Jr., Esq., 
City Solicitor. 
 
The Committee conducted a public input period, at which there were no speakers. 
 
 
The Committee took up the following: 
 
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO ENTER INTO A LEASE AGREEMENT 
WITH JOSHUA CAFÉ, LLC  D/B/A NEWS CAFÉ FOR A TERM OF SIX (6) MONTHS 
FOLLOWED BY A MONTH-TO-MONTH TENANCY FOR THE PARKING AREA LOT 
FRONTING ON BROAD STREET AND NORTH UNION STREET 
 
The committee reviewed the lease agreement.  There were no issues, 
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Araujo, seconded by Councilor Stachowiak, the Committee 
recommended APPROVAL of this resolution on a roll call vote, as follows: 
 
AYES – Councilor Stachowiak, Chair; Councilors Araujo and Moreno. 
 
NOES – 0. 
 
 
The Committee took up the following: 
 
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET TO ENTER INTO AN 
EASEMENT AGREEMENT WITH NARRAGANSETT ELECTRIC COMPANY TO 
MAINTAIN AN UNDERGROUND DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM FOR THE PROPERTY 
LOCATED AT 100 FREIGHT STREET (ASSESSOR’S PLAT 8, LOT 417) 
 
The committee reviewed the easement agreement. 
 
Mr. Milos stated that he made the changes to the easement agreement, which were approved by the 
committee and sent it to the Narragansett Electric Company for their review.  He stated that he was 
copied on an e-mail stating that the RI Energy right of way team was in possession of the proposed 
changes and was looking into them. As of Wednesday, neither he nor Mr. Crawley had received a 
direct response to the changes.
City Property Committee 
October 21, 2026 
Page 2 
 
The committee, noting that the matter is time sensitive , decided to vote on the resolution with the 
following understanding – If Narragansett Electric has issues with any of the proposed changes, 
Mr. Milos will negotiate with them to resolve the concerns.  If the changes are minor, he will make 
the changes.  If he believes the cha nges are major, he will bring the matter back to the committee 
for a new vote on the agreement. 
  
Upon motion made by Councilor Araujo, seconded by Councilor Stachowiak, the Committee 
recommended APPROVAL of this resolution on a roll call vote, as follows: 
 
AYES – Councilor Stachowiak, Chair; Councilors Araujo and Moreno. 
 
NOES – 0. 
 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 6:43 p.m. 
 
 
 
Richard J. Goldstein, MMC, Clerk 
Pawtucket City Council
